pages.text: "No bath!" Lulu scurried behind the barn. Warm water filled the wooden tub in the yard. Three cousins were already sitting inside.
"Water on my head stings!" Lulu stayed hidden. The cousins splashed and called.
But sitting behind the barn, Lulu felt sticky. Rolling in the field had left dust all through the fur. "My back keeps itching!" Lulu scratched the neck and rubbed the side.
Aunt Rosa, who made everything big, arrived in a headscarf with an armful of soap. "Forget a bath, Lulu. Want to make a bubble hat?" "A bubble hat? What is that?" Lulu's eyes widened.
Aunt Rosa stirred the water and rubbed soap. Foam rose above the tub in a white mountain. "Wow! Taller than me!" Lulu's eyes sparkled.
"A hat needs steps," she whispered. "Splash in, put on a bubble hat, rinse with water!" Lulu stamped excitedly. "Quick, Aunt Rosa!"
Lulu splashed into the middle of the tub. Aunt Rosa piled bubbles on the head. The cousins laughed in their own bubble hats. "Bubble hats and splashes!"
Water washed the bubbles down. Wet fur lay flat, and the itchy back felt fresh. Lulu put the bell cord back round the neck. Jingle!
Next evening, Lulu ran to the tub first. "One, splash in! Two, bubble hat! Three, rinse with water!" The cousins followed in a line.
Aunt Rosa wrapped Lulu in a big towel and hugged tight. A bath was exciting water play instead of something scary. "Bubble hats and splashes! Make mine bigger tomorrow, Aunt Rosa!"
